To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the degradation pathways of the GnRH analog buserelin by the rat kidney are different from those by the rat liver.
buserelin is degraded by the kidney membrane fraction to a large extent by aminopeptides, which are inhibited by amastatin and by a dipeptidyl peptidase, which is inhibited by bestatin.

Buserelin is degraded by the kidney membrane to the peptides B1-2 (pGlu-Hist), B1-3 (pGlu- His- Trp) and B6-8 (Ser- Tyr- D-Ser- Leu-Arg) and the amino acids Tyr and Trp, which are released from the C-terminal and N-terminal fragments, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation of the GnRH analog buserelin in rat kidney membranes and the pathways of the enzymatic degradation of the GnRh analog buserelin.
the development of a method for the determination of the total amount of buserelin in plasma.
the study of the degradation of GnRH analogs in the kidney, which is one of the main organs of their metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
buserelin is degraded by the rat kidney microsomal membrane to the N-terminal fragments B1-2 (B1-3, 1-4), the C-terminal fragments B5-9 (B6-9) and B4-9 (B3-4) and the amino acids Tyr and Trp.
the kidney membrane fraction degrades B1-9 in the following order of preference: B1-2 > B6-9 > B1-3 > B1-9 > B5-9 > B4- 9 > B3.9 > B3 4.

buserelin was degraded by the rat kidney to the following peptide products: B1-4 (pGlu-Hir-Trp-Ser), B1-3 (pGlu- His-Trp), B1-2 (pGlu), B1-9 (Buserelin) and B3-9 (His-Trp-Ser- Tyr-D-Ser(tbu)-Leu-arginine), B4-9 (His-Tyr-D-Sera(tbu)-
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the kidney membrane fraction is capable of hydrolyzing the GnRH analog buserelin into the N-terminal fragments B1-3 and B1-2 (and the amino acids Ser, Tyr, Trp) as well as the C-terminal fragments B5-9 and B6-10 (and the amino acid Ser).
the kidney is the major organ for degradation of buserlin and that the major pathway for the inactivation of buserlin is its hydrolysis to the C-terminal peptide B6-9.

the degradation pathways of the GnRH analogs in the kidney membrane fraction were very similar to those in the kidney cortex slices and in the kidney homogenate and, therefore, the membrane preparation was a very suitable model for the study of the pathways of degradation of the GnRH antagonists in the kidney tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degradation of the GnRH analogs by the membrane fraction of rat kidney is a rather complex process.
the kidney is an important organ of the metabolism of buserelin, which may have implications on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of this GnRH analog.
the degradation pathway of buserelin in kidney is different from that in plasma and that the kidney is the main organ responsible for the formation of the metabolites B1-2.
